clue.text: Best time almost to wear a gem

indicators.note: a gem worn by something has that thing on it, so the stone's letters go around the other piece

parts.note: an opal is a gem

indicators.note: almost means the word stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as the word itself before trimming

explanation.surface: Advice on the ideal moment to put on a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final E of the word for time, and 'to wear' wraps the gem around what is left. 'wear' suggests putting on jewellery, but here the gem does the wearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal and best are synonyms: the most favourable possible.

clue.text: Well-behaved hospital worker

explanation.surface: A model employee on the wards.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderly means tidy and disciplined; an orderly is also an attendant doing routine jobs in a hospital.

clue.text: "Twist and shout" succeeded for many

indicators.note: to twist something is to distort it out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A famous rock-and-roll song title, apparently a hit with the masses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' rearranges AND SHOUT to make THOUSAND; S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Thousands is a loose way of saying a great many, a large number.

clue.text: Cleric turned up around one in the city

indicators.note: the cleric's word goes around the numeral piece
in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an imam is a Muslim cleric who leads prayers
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A clergyman pitches up somewhere in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts I inside IMAM to give IMAIM, and 'turned up' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a city in Florida.

clue.text: Realised king not disheartened

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

indicators.note: disheartened means losing its heart, so only the outer letters of the word stay

explanation.surface: A monarch understood something without losing courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the middle O from NOT, leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: To have learnt something is to have found it out, realised it.

clue.text: Is inquisitive about case of single malt for ministers

indicators.note: 'about' puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: someone who pries is inquisitive, being nosy

indicators.note: the case of something is its outside, so take the first and last letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A nosy person wonders about a bottle of whisky's packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes S and T, the first and last letters of 'single malt'; 'about' is a link meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: Priests are ministers of religion, members of the clergy.

clue.text: Private parking near new Orleans

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A private car park close to the newer part of New Orleans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' looks like part of the city name New Orleans, but it is the anagram signal working on Orleans alone; 'near' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal and private both mean belonging to one individual, not public.

clue.text: Nouveau vin stolen in bust

indicators.note: nouveau means new, so the letters of the words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Fresh French wine pinched during a police raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nouveau' is the anagram signal, borrowed from Beaujolais Nouveau, and 'bust' means broke rather than a police raid.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bust has no money left, unable to pay debts.

clue.text: Jack, perhaps, is in short, behind

indicators.note: in short means the word is shortened, cut down as in a contraction

parts.note: prat is slang for the buttocks

explanation.surface: Jack is, briefly, at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' cuts IS to its contracted form 'S. Jack Sprat is the nursery-rhyme man who could eat no fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Sprat of the nursery rhyme is one bearer of the name, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Like August, say, in brief statement announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a summary is a brief statement of the main points

explanation.surface: A short statement made public about the month of August.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMMARY and SUMMERY sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: August is a month of the warm season, so it is typical of that season.

clue.text: Am radio broadcast museum feature

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: An AM radio programme on displays in a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges AM RADIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scene with modelled figures, often found in museums.

clue.text: Platform used by odd sort in odd surroundings

indicators.note: in, with surroundings after it, puts the scrambled piece inside the other
surroundings describes the outer piece wrapping around the inner one

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange

indicators.note: odd here means strange, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stage used by a strange type in peculiar settings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... surroundings' is split by the second 'odd', which is the outer piece. RUM is old British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised stand for a speaker or conductor.

clue.text: See out trial runs? Impossible in this game

indicators.note: impossible signals that the letters cannot stay as they are and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting through practice runs is impossible in a deadly game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impossible' rearranges SEE OUT TRIAL RUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: The game in question is the deadly gamble of a revolver with one loaded chamber, which a player may not see out.

clue.text: Moscow party member with number unknown over there

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the whole run of letters reads backwards

parts.note: a red is a Communist, as of the party once ruling from Moscow
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A Soviet Communist with an undetermined figure, standing far away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses RED NO Y as one run. 'over there' looks like the definition, but 'over' is needed for the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonder is a dated word for at that place, at a distance.

clue.text: Midshipman not staying relaxed

parts.note: Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Frederick Marryat's 1836 novel
someone not staying is going, leaving

explanation.surface: A junior naval officer leaves in a calm frame of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue relies on the title character of Marryat's novel Mr Midshipman Easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Easygoing describes a relaxed, tolerant temperament.

clue.text: Go to arrest a nuisance for hanging!

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold or seize, so the first piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: a go is a try, an attempt
a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: An instruction to detain a troublemaker for execution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to arrest' wraps the attempt around A and the nuisance. 'hanging' means a wall hanging, not an execution.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven textile hung on a wall as decoration.

clue.text: Nice heads keeping adult in conversation

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the heads hold the letter for adult

parts.note: Nice is the French city, so heads are given in French, the word for head twice
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: French heads of state hold a grown-up in discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, signalling French. 'keeping' puts A between the two TETEs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a private talk between two people, literally head to head.

clue.text: Start on course with range adjusted for youngster

parts.note: on a golf course each hole starts from the tee

indicators.note: adjusted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer begins a round after adjusting their driving range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start on course' points to golf, where play on each hole begins at the tee; 'adjusted' rearranges the range.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is a young person aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Asteroids could produce this, nothing less

definitions.text: Asteroids could produce this, nothing less

indicators.note: could produce suggests the letters may be worked into something new
less means without, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: O is the round figure for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: An impact from space rocks would cause catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing less' removes O from ASTEROIDS, and 'could produce' rearranges the rest; the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid strike is a classic image of a catastrophe.

clue.text: Plots some French put across in g & s medley

parts.note: des is French for some

indicators.note: a medley is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Schemes of the French put into a Gilbert and Sullivan medley.
explanation.walkthrough: G & S suggests Gilbert and Sullivan; here the two letters join IN in the mix that 'medley' signals. 'put across' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Designs and plots are both schemes or intentions.

clue.text: Rank university in figures

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for figures

parts.note: stats is short for statistics, figures

explanation.surface: University rankings appear in league tables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U inside STATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is a person's standing or position in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Hawking pet hens is wrong

indicators.note: is wrong signals the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone peddling pet chickens is misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawking' means the physicist Stephen Hawking, not selling.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen was the first name of the physicist Hawking.

clue.text: Said to be attractive carriage

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: handsome means attractive

explanation.surface: A coach is reported to be good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: HANDSOME, said aloud, sounds like HANSOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom is a two-wheeled horse-drawn cab.

clue.text: Match report would follow this event?

definitions.text: Match report would follow this event?

parts.words: Match report would follow this event?
parts.note: match read as a wedding and report as the bang of a firearm: a forced wedding, prompted by a threat of gunfire

explanation.surface: A newspaper write-up after a football game.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests sport journalism; the cryptic reading turns match into a wedding and report into a gunshot.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding forced on a couple, traditionally by the bride's father armed with a gun, because she is pregnant.

clue.text: M east national upset in a short time

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: in a mo, short for a moment, means in a short time

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern citizen gets upset quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'M east' stands for Middle East. 'upset' reverses IN A MO.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani is a citizen of Oman, a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Short run by river in the country

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
the Ural is a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian Sea

explanation.surface: A quick jog beside a river in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: R and URAL join.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means relating to the countryside rather than the town.

clue.text: Harsh assessment by head of government

indicators.note: by means next to, so the first letter of government is placed beside the assessment
head of means the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a rating is an assessment or grading

explanation.surface: A critical review of a political leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives G, placed in front of RATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Grating means rasping and unpleasant on the ear, harsh.

clue.text: Cry coming from unruly creches

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Noise from rowdy nurseries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges CRECHES.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a loud shrill shout or cry.

clue.text: Lively guy involving women in lark?

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the bird's word wraps around the letter

parts.note: a lark is a songbird, so a singer

explanation.surface: A fun-loving man gets women caught up in a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lark' looks like a prank but is the bird; 'involving' puts W inside SINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A swinger is a fashionable, fun-loving person who enjoys an active social life.

clue.text: Think about one German plant

parts.note: to mull over something is to think about it
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: Consider a single German plant.
explanation.walkthrough: MULL and EIN join.
explanation.definitionFit: Mullein is a tall plant with woolly leaves and yellow flower spikes.
